audio.t: Did you get enough people to fill out your survey on campus food?

questions.explain: 問問卷是否已收集到足夠填答者，C 表示快了、還差約二十份，最合理。A 重複 food 談價格；B 以 filled up 混淆 fill out，答非所問。
options: Yes, the food here is pretty cheap.
I filled up my water bottle already.
Almost. I still need about twenty more responses.

audio.t: Do we need approval from the ethics committee before we interview the students?

questions.explain: 問訪談前是否需倫理委員會核准，A 回答需要並說明審查時間，最合理。B 重複 committee；C 重複 interview 但指求職面試，皆答非所問。
options: Yes, and the review can take up to two weeks.
The committee meeting was a lot of fun.
I'll interview for the job on Friday.

audio.t: Why is the consent form so long?

questions.explain: Why 問原因，B 說明同意書須解釋所有可能風險，最合理。A 回答位置；C 回答所需時間，誤把 so long 當成 how long。
options: I think it's in the second folder.
Because it has to explain every possible risk to participants.
About ten minutes, if you read quickly.

audio.t: Professor Lin, I posted my survey link in a few class group chats, but only fifteen people have answered so far.
That's quite low. Did you mention how long it takes? Students are much more willing to help when they know it's only five minutes.
I didn't. I'll add that and post it again tonight.

questions.explain: 男生最後說 I'll add that and post it again tonight，that 指填答所需時間，故選 B。對話未提延期、現金獎勵或訪談，fifteen 只是目前填答人數。
options: Ask the professor to extend the deadline.
Repost the survey with the expected completion time.
Offer participants a cash reward.
Interview fifteen more students.
questions.prompt: What will the man most likely do tonight?

audio.t: Kevin, I noticed your survey asks for students' full names and ID numbers.
I wanted to make sure nobody answered twice.
I understand, but you don't need that much personal data. Just turn on the one response per account setting and keep the survey anonymous.

questions.explain: 女生說 you don't need that much personal data，並建議保持匿名，故選 C。B 是男生想預防的情況，並非已發生；A 未提及。
options: The survey is too short.
Some students have already answered twice.
The survey collects unnecessary personal information.
questions.prompt: What is the woman's main concern?

audio.t: Attention, all students. The Department of Psychology is looking for volunteers for a study on sleep and memory. Participants will spend about forty minutes in the lab on the third floor of the Social Sciences Building and will receive two hundred New Taiwan dollars as a thank you. To sign up, please scan the QR code on the poster outside Room three oh five. Spots are limited to sixty people.

questions.explain: 廣播說參與者將獲得 two hundred New Taiwan dollars as a thank you，即小額現金，故選 D。學分、睡眠報告與工作坊皆未提及，sleep、memory 只是研究主題。
options: Extra course credit.
A free sleep test report.
A spot in a memory workshop.
A small cash payment.

audio.t: Before you start collecting data for your final projects, I want to go over a few ethical rules. First, every participant must give informed consent. That means you explain what the study is about, how long it will take, and what you will do with their answers before they agree to take part. They should also know they can stop at any time without any penalty.

Second, protect people's privacy. Unless you truly need it, don't collect names, phone numbers, or student ID numbers. Store your data on the university's cloud drive, not on a personal laptop or a USB stick, and delete the raw data after the semester ends.

Finally, if your project involves anyone under eighteen, or asks about sensitive topics such as health or family problems, you must submit your plan to the research ethics office first. The review usually takes about ten working days, so please don't wait until the last minute. If you're not sure whether your project needs a review, email me by this Friday.

questions.explain: 教授開頭即說 I want to go over a few ethical rules，之後依序說明知情同意、隱私與送審，故選 B。未談資料分析、期限或介紹人員。
options: To explain how to analyze survey data.
To review ethical rules for collecting data.
To announce the final project deadline.
To introduce the staff of the research ethics office.
questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the talk?

questions.explain: 教授說 Store your data on the university's cloud drive, not on a personal laptop or a USB stick，故選 C；A、B 正是被排除的選項。
options: On a personal laptop.
On a USB stick.
On the university's cloud drive.
In the professor's office.
questions.prompt: According to the speaker, where should students store their data?

questions.explain: 教授指出涉及未滿十八歲者，或詢問健康、家庭問題等敏感主題的專題須先送審，故選 B、E。ten working days 是審查所需時間，非送審條件；A、D 未提及。
options: Projects that use the university's cloud drive.
Projects involving participants under eighteen.
Projects lasting more than ten working days.
Projects with fewer than fifty responses.
Projects that ask about family problems.
questions.prompt: Which projects must be submitted to the research ethics office? (Choose TWO.)

questions.explain: agreeing to be recorded 表示同意，consent form 為「同意書」，故選 C。complaint（抱怨）、contest（比賽）、concert（音樂會）拼字相近但語意不合。
options: complaint
contest
consent
concert
questions.prompt: Before the interview began, each participant signed a ______ form agreeing to be recorded.

questions.explain: To protect students' privacy 提示應不具名，anonymous（匿名的）最合適，故選 D。available（可取得的）反而不利隱私；enormous、ambitious 語意不合。
options: enormous
ambitious
available
anonymous
questions.prompt: To protect students' privacy, the researchers kept all survey responses completely ______.

head: From: Research Ethics Office <ethics@hsinchu-u.edu.tw>
To: All Undergraduate Students
Subject: New Online System for Student Research Review
passage: Starting December 1, all applications for research ethics review must be submitted through our new online system instead of by email. The system allows you to upload your consent form and questionnaire, track the status of your application, and receive comments from reviewers directly.

Please note that projects for course assignments do not need a full review if they are anonymous and involve only adults. However, you must still complete a short self-check form, which takes about five minutes. Projects involving minors, medical information, or audio and video recordings require a full review, which typically takes ten working days.
A one-hour workshop on using the new system will be held on November 27 at 2 p.m. in Room 204 of the Administration Building. Seats are limited, so please register in advance on our office website.

questions.explain: 首段說明自 12 月 1 日起申請須改用新的線上系統而非電子郵件，故選 D。工作坊是舉辦而非取消；未提期限或招募審查員。
options: To remind students of the final project deadline.
To recruit students to serve as reviewers.
To cancel an upcoming workshop.
To announce a new way to submit applications.
questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of the email?

questions.explain: 信中指出涉及 audio and video recordings 的研究需完整審查，故選 A。匿名且僅限成人的課堂作業只需填自我檢核表；five minutes 指檢核表所需時間。
options: A study that records interviews on video.
An anonymous survey of adult classmates.
A class project with only adult volunteers.
A questionnaire that takes five minutes to finish.
questions.prompt: Which project would most likely require a full review?

questions.explain: track the status of your application 指追蹤申請進度，與 follow 意思最接近，故選 C。design、delete、print 都無法搭配 status 表達「掌握進度」。
options: design
delete
follow
print
questions.prompt: The word "track" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to

passage: Every December, students at Taiwanese universities receive a flood of survey links. Classmates need data for final projects, graduate students are finishing their theses, and campus offices want feedback on their services. According to a recent study by the student union, the average undergraduate received eleven survey requests in the last three weeks of the fall semester. Researchers call the result "survey fatigue": people become so tired of questionnaires that they ignore them or rush through them without reading.

Survey fatigue is more than an annoyance. When fewer people respond, the results may not represent the whole student body. Worse, participants who answer quickly and carelessly can make the data unreliable. "A survey with three hundred careless answers is less useful than one with eighty thoughtful ones," says Dr. Grace Huang, who teaches research methods in the Department of Sociology.

Dr. Huang offers several suggestions for student researchers. First, keep questionnaires short; she recommends no more than fifteen questions. Second, be honest about the time required. Third, explain clearly why the research matters, since people are more willing to help when they understand the purpose. She also warns against offering large prizes, because they may attract participants who care only about the reward.

The student union is now testing a new approach. Instead of posting links in dozens of group chats, students can list their surveys on a single campus research board, where volunteers choose the studies that interest them. Early results are encouraging: surveys on the board have received more complete answers than those shared through social media.

questions.explain: 全文先說明問卷疲乏現象與影響，再提出黃教授的建議與學生會的新做法，故選 C。文中反對大獎品，D 與原文相反；A、B 只是枝節。
options: The history of the student union.
How to design a graduate thesis.
A problem caused by too many survey requests and ways to deal with it.
Why prizes improve survey response rates.
questions.prompt: What is the article mainly about?

questions.explain: 第二段指出草率作答 can make the data unreliable，黃教授也說三百份草率答案不如八十份用心的答案，故選 B。其餘選項文中未提。
options: They make surveys take longer to finish.
They make the data less reliable.
They break university rules.
They cost researchers extra money.
questions.prompt: According to Dr. Huang, why are careless answers a problem?

questions.explain: 末段說明研究看板上 volunteers choose the studies that interest them，故選 D。看板由學生會試辦，非社會系；文中未限研究生，也未提供大獎品。
options: It is run by the Department of Sociology.
It is only open to graduate students.
It offers large prizes to participants.
It lets volunteers choose the studies they want to join.
questions.prompt: What is true about the campus research board?

questions.explain: 第三段建議題目不超過十五題，並清楚說明研究的重要性，故選 A、D。她反對大獎品（C）；B 是學生會想取代的做法；E 未提及。
options: Limit a questionnaire to about fifteen questions.
Post survey links in as many group chats as possible.
Offer large prizes to attract more people.
Explain why the research is important.
Send surveys only in December.
questions.prompt: Which are suggestions that Dr. Huang gives to student researchers? (Choose TWO.)

words.ex: Researchers must get informed consent before collecting any data.
The survey is anonymous, so no one will know how you answered.
Each participant will receive two hundred dollars as a thank-you.
Please keep your questionnaire under fifteen questions.
Studies involving minors require a full ethics review.
Participants can withdraw at any time without penalty.
Careless answers can make survey data less reliable.
You can track the status of your application online.
